sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Homeopathy, a system of medicine developed in the 18th century, has gained increasing popularity in India as an alternative to conventional treatments. Based on the principle of “like cures like,” it employs highly diluted substances to stimulate the body’s natural healing mechanisms. Advocates claim efficacy in chronic conditions, minor ailments, and as complementary therapy alongside allopathy. Despite widespread use, homeopathy faces criticism due to a lack of empirical evidence, challenges in standardization, and debates over placebo effects. Regulatory frameworks in India aim to ensure quality control, professional training, and integration with national health programs. Patient preference, cultural acceptance, and affordability contribute to its continued growth. Emerging research explores homeopathy’s potential mechanisms, safety profiles, and role in holistic health, suggesting that its future hinges on reconciling traditional practice with scientific scrutiny.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Biological medicine, encompassing vaccines, monoclonal antibodies, and gene therapies, represents a rapidly advancing frontier in India’s healthcare sector. Its development relies on sophisticated research infrastructure, stringent regulatory frameworks, and skilled scientific personnel. The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted both India’s capacity for rapid vaccine production and the systemic challenges of equitable distribution. Biological therapeutics are often expensive and require cold-chain logistics, limiting accessibility in rural and low-income regions. Ethical concerns arise regarding clinical trials, informed consent, and long-term safety monitoring. Collaboration between government institutions, private companies, and international agencies has facilitated innovation, knowledge transfer, and scaling of production. Despite progress, gaps in public awareness, healthcare infrastructure, and affordability continue to restrict the full potential of biological medicine, underscoring the tension between scientific advancement and social equity.

questions.q: The passage primarily portrays homeopathy as
opts: a scientifically proven replacement for allopathy
an alternative system with cultural and practical relevance
questions.why: It is called an alternative with growing popularity, cultural acceptance and affordability. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: The phrase “like cures like” refers to
opts: using diluted substances to trigger natural healing
questions.why: The next clause explains it: diluted substances stimulate natural healing. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which criticism of homeopathy is explicitly mentioned?
opts: Lack of empirical evidence and standardization
questions.why: Stated directly in the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: What factor contributes to the continued popularity of homeopathy in India?
opts: Cultural acceptance, affordability, and patient preference
questions.why: Listed word for word in the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: The author’s overall perspective on homeopathy is
opts: analytical, highlighting both potential and limitations
questions.why: The passage weighs growth against criticism and ends on scientific scrutiny. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: The passage primarily presents biological medicine in India as
opts: a high-tech, evolving medical frontier with challenges
questions.why: A “rapidly advancing frontier” that still faces cost, access and ethical gaps. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which factor most limits access to biological medicine in rural areas?
questions.why: Cost and cold-chain needs are said to limit rural access. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Ethical concerns mentioned in the passage primarily relate to
questions.why: Stated in the fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: How does collaboration impact biological medicine in India?
opts: It facilitates innovation, scaling, and knowledge transfer
questions.why: Stated in the sixth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: The overall tone of the passage is
questions.why: It credits progress and lists the gaps. Passage: GPSC CBRT (State Tax Officer), Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The authority ordered him to submit the documents.”
opts: He was ordered to submit the documents.
He is ordered to submit the documents.
He was ordered submitting the documents.
To submit the documents was ordered to him.
questions.why: Past active becomes 'was ordered'; the infinitive 'to submit' stays. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: If I was the director, I would approve the funding.
If I were the director, I would approve the funding.
If I am the director, I would approve the funding.
If I had been the director, I approve the funding.
questions.why: Unreal present: 'If I were …, I would …'. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “The seminar is optional; you ____ attend if you are occupied.”
questions.why: 'Needn't' means there is no obligation. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct inverted structure:
opts: Scarcely she had stepped outside when the storm began.
Scarcely had she stepped outside when the storm began.
Scarcely had she stepped outside than the storm began.
Scarcely did she stepped outside when the storm began.
questions.why: Scarcely + had + subject … when. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct question tag: “Let’s go for a walk, ____?”
questions.why: Sentences beginning with 'Let's' take the tag 'shall we?'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Which Indian city was the only one listed in the Work From Anywhere Index 2026?
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, which completed six years in September 2026, is for the:
Who were named ICC Players of the Month for September 2026?
The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 were held in which country?
questions.why: 19 September to 4 October 2026.

questions.q: The theme of Ayurveda Day 2026 (23 September) was:
The 'Churches and Convents of Goa' were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
questions.why: Includes the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral.

questions.q: The new series of India's national accounts uses which base year?
The grand finale of the Bharatiya Antariksh Hackathon 2026 was held at the NRSC, which is in:
questions.why: National Remote Sensing Centre. Aug 2026.

questions.q: The 36th Ig Nobel Prize ceremony (2026) was held, for the first time in 35 years, outside the USA, in:
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:
questions.why: W. C. Bonnerjee presided over the first session in Bombay.

questions.q: Statement: Sales of a product have fallen sharply. Courses of action: I. Study rival products in the market. II. Cut the price and improve quality.
questions.why: Study comes first; II prescribes a remedy before the cause is known. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.

questions.q: Parents have complained of bullying during recess. Which situation should the recess aides report to the principal?
opts: Four girls surround another and hold her backpack
Two boys argue over a basketball score
Three boys play a banned video game
questions.why: Only B shows a group intimidating one child. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2024.

questions.q: A Five-Day Suspension is for (1) physically assaulting someone or (2) wilfully damaging or defacing school property. Which is the best example?
opts: Lillian is caught cheating a second time
Marc is sent out for disruptions
Franny spray-paints insults on the locker-room wall and is suspended
Failing students must stay for tutoring
questions.why: Defacing school property meets condition (2). GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: A town's population grew from 1,75,000 to 2,62,500 in a decade. What was the average per cent increase per year?
questions.why: Increase 87,500 = 50% over 10 years: 5% a year on average (simple). GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: Should trade unions be banned completely? I. Yes, workers can concentrate on production. II. No, it is the only way employees can put demands to management. III. Yes, unions get illegal demands met. IV. No, advanced countries don't ban them.
opts: Only I and II are strong
Only I, II and III are strong
questions.why: II gives a real, important reason. I and III are weak generalisations; IV just copies others. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: Rainfall in the catchment was below normal for two months, yet the city's water supply has not been cut. Assumptions: I. Rainfall later in the monsoon may be adequate. II. Present lake levels may be adequate for normal supply.
opts: Either I or II is implicit
questions.why: Not cutting supply assumes enough water now and the hope of more later. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: What day of the week was 15 August 1947?
questions.why: Independence Day 1947 fell on a Friday. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Sara lives in a large East Coast city. Her younger cousin Marlee lives in a small Mid-west town. Marlee has visited Sara several times in five years; Sara has visited Marlee once. Which must be true?
questions.why: Marlee is the younger cousin, so Sara is older. The rest is speculation. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Statement: Schools have multiplied, but most are ill-equipped and not excellent. Conclusions: I. We should give these schools good teachers and equipment. II. We need not open more schools.
questions.why: The problem stated is quality, which I addresses; II goes beyond the statement. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: At what time between 4 and 5 o’clock will the hands of the clock be together?
questions.why: 5.5M = 120, so M = 21 9/11 min ≈ 21 min 49 s. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Treating a disease with the very agent or product that caused it is called:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hahnemann discussed isopathy in a note to §56 and did not accept it as true homoeopathy.

questions.q: Diseases presenting only one or two striking symptoms, which hide the rest of the picture, are called by Hahnemann:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §172–173; they are hard to cure because the picture is incomplete.

questions.q: According to Kent, a remedy that produces new symptoms in the patient was:
opts: only partially similar, so the case needs restudy
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Kent's ninth observation: new symptoms mean the remedy was not well chosen.

questions.q: A sycotic remedy with fixed ideas, warts, and the sensation of something alive moving in the abdomen is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Thuja's fixed ideas and sensation of something alive in the abdomen.

questions.q: A great desire for fresh air, burning pains relieved by heat, and offensive, foul-smelling discharges with a history of never being well since a suppressed eruption suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Psorinum: chilly, offensive, despair of recovery; 'never well since'.

questions.q: Profuse, watery, painless diarrhoea with marked prostration, cold sweat on the forehead and collapse calls for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Veratrum album: cold sweat on the forehead, collapse.

questions.q: Sensation of a plug in various parts, sweet taste, and complaints relieved by eating are characteristic of:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Anacardium: the plug sensation, relief from eating, two wills.

questions.q: The vehicle used to prepare mother tinctures from fresh plants is:
opts: Purified alcohol (strong alcohol or dispensing alcohol)
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Alcohol of the strength laid down in the HPI.

questions.q: Globules used in homoeopathy are made of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Sugar-of-milk is used for triturations and tablets; globules are cane sugar.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, the rubric for 'fear of death' is found in the chapter:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. All mental symptoms are under Mind.

questions.q: Boger's 'Synoptic Key' is best described as:
opts: a concise repertory with a materia medica section
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Boger's Synoptic Key to the Materia Medica, with a repertory part.

questions.q: The 'anatomical snuffbox' contains the pulsation of the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Scaphoid fractures cause tenderness here.

questions.q: The hormone that regulates blood calcium and is secreted by the parathyroid glands is:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. It raises serum calcium.

questions.q: Repair by replacement with fibrous tissue, as after a myocardial infarct, is called:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Cardiac muscle cannot regenerate.

questions.q: The Mantoux test detects:
opts: hypersensitivity to tuberculoprotein (past or present infection)
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. A positive test does not by itself mean active disease.

questions.q: The commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia is:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. The pneumococcus.

questions.q: A remedy for diabetes with marked thirst, dry mouth and copious urine, often prescribed in mother tincture as a 'specific', is:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Syzygium is a classical organ remedy for diabetes.

questions.q: Painful, red, swollen great toe joint at night with exquisite sensitivity to touch suggests homoeopathically:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Colchicum for acute gout; smell of food causes nausea.

questions.q: The first stage of labour ends with:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. First stage: from true labour pains to full dilatation.

questions.q: Bed-wetting in a child older than five years is called:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Nocturnal enuresis.

questions.q: A partial-thickness burn with blisters is classed as:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Full-thickness burns are painless and need grafting.

questions.q: Opacity of the lens of the eye is called:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Commonest cause of treatable blindness.

questions.q: The incidence of a disease measures:
opts: all existing cases at a point in time
new cases occurring in a defined period
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Prevalence counts all existing cases.

questions.q: Rigor mortis first appears in the:
opts: Myocardium (and then the eyelids and face)
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Heart first, then eyelids, face, and downward (Nysten's rule).

questions.q: In medical ethics, 'informed consent' requires that the patient:
opts: understands the nature, risks and alternatives of the procedure and agrees voluntarily
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Consent must be informed, voluntary and given by a competent person.
